nodes.label: Attention-Only Transformers and Implementing MLPs with Attention Heads
nodes.author: Robert Huben, Valerie Morris
nodes.rationale: Theoretical work proving MLPs can be implemented as masked attention heads with internal dimension 1, enabling conversion of standard transformers to attention-only architectures.

nodes.label: MLP-Attention Head Equivalence
nodes.rationale: Theorem 3 proves MLP neurons with generalized SiLU activation can be implemented by masked attention heads using bias token and special masking pattern.

nodes.label: Attention-Only Transformer Conversion
nodes.rationale: Theorem 6 shows entire transformer can be converted to attention-only by replacing MLP layers with attention heads, though at cost of exponentially more heads.

nodes.label: Separate Linear and Activation Functions
nodes.rationale: Theorems 7-8 prove attention heads can separately implement row-wise linear transformations and entry-wise activation functions.

nodes.label: Masking Pattern Encoding in Weights
nodes.rationale: Theorem 9 shows arbitrary masking patterns can be encoded in WQK weight matrices to arbitrary precision by augmenting residual stream with identity matrix.

nodes.label: Transformer Architecture
nodes.rationale: Standard architecture with alternating attention and MLP sublayers, layer normalization, and skip connections. Foundation for all three papers' work.

nodes.label: Generalized SiLU Activation Function
nodes.rationale: Function class a1*SiLU(a2*x) that includes SiLU and close approximations of ReLU and GeLU. Required for MLP-attention equivalence proofs.

nodes.label: Masked Softmax Function
nodes.rationale: Row-wise softmax applied only to unmasked entries. Core operation in masked attention heads used for MLP implementation.

nodes.label: Bias Token Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Special persistent vector appended to residual stream to enable MLP implementation. Similar to persistent memory vectors in prior work.

nodes.label: Mechanistic Interpretability
nodes.rationale: Research direction seeking human-understandable explanations of transformer computations. Attention-only conversion enables applying interpretability techniques to MLP layers.
